transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I've been getting really focused on some things about how I look lately. I work in production, and since I started helping out with the safety trainings, I just can’t seem to stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out to the others. 

It really bothers me, and it doesn't just stop at my hands. I also start thinking my face looks crooked in the company newsletter photos. I've brought it up, and other people say they don’t see it at all, but I just can't seem to let it go. I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Do you find yourself repeatedly doing things like checking your appearance in mirrors, comparing yourself to others, or trying to hide your hands and face?

Yes, I do find myself doing that. Especially before I help with a safety class, or... well, even before a workshop at the senior center. I'll go into the bathroom and check the mirror a few times. I always make sure to put extra lotion on my hands, and I'll turn my face different ways just to see how it looks. 

Sometimes I even ask a coworker if I look all right before I go out there. It makes me run a little behind schedule sometimes, doing all of that, but I still get myself there.
If you felt completely satisfied with how your hands and face looked, would you still feel anxious or uncomfortable being around others or leading those trainings?

No, I don't think I would. I actually really enjoy doing the trainings and being around my coworkers. If I didn't have this... this hang-up about how my hands and face look, I'd be completely fine. It really is just that specific thing that makes me uncomfortable.
